level_1.description: Rename SSA variables using inspection-derived symbol table
rules: Use ONLY variable names identified in inspection results
Rename ALL SSA values exactly once using a deterministic mapping
Do NOT modify op names such as torch.add, torch.mm, torch.relu, etc.
Do NOT change tensor types or ranks
Preserve use-def chains strictly as defined in inspection graph
Ensure SSA dominance rules are maintained
Do NOT introduce new variables or remove existing ones
Result must pass mlir-opt with torch dialect enabled

level_1.description: Reorder independent operations using inspection dependency graph
rules: Use ONLY dependency graph from inspection results
Reorder ONLY operations explicitly marked independent
Do NOT reorder operations involving side-effects or mutation
Do NOT move operations across blocks or regions
Ensure all operands are defined before use
Do NOT infer independence beyond inspection data
No insertion or deletion of operations
Use inspection ordering as the ONLY valid program structure; do NOT reorder operations, blocks, or regions
Preserve ALL torch operations exactly, including full op names such as torch.add, torch.aten.mm, torch.relu, etc.
Do NOT modify ANY attributes including dtype, device, layout, requires_grad, or memory format
Preserve tensor types EXACTLY including rank, shape, dtype, and optional attributes
Ensure SSA values are consistently named and referenced; no dangling or duplicate names allowed
Preserve block arguments and region arguments EXACTLY; argument counts, order, and types must match
Ensure every SSA value is defined before use according to dominance rules
Normalize formatting ONLY (whitespace, indentation, line breaks, attribute spacing)
At least ONE formatting-level transformation MUST be applied to ensure output is textually different
Valid transformations include: renaming temporary SSA values, reformatting numeric literals, or canonical spacing changes
Do NOT introduce new operations, constants, attributes, or regions
Do NOT remove any existing operations, arguments, or attributes
Output MUST be syntactically different from input AND pass torch-mlir-opt pipeline successfully

level_1.description: Apply deterministic SSA renaming using inspection metadata
rules: Ensure consistent renaming across all uses

level_1.description: Reconstruct program strictly from inspection graph
rules: Reconstruct the program using ONLY nodes and edges present in inspection metadata
Preserve EXACT operation ordering, including intra-block and inter-block ordering
Ensure all SSA values are reconstructed with correct definitions before uses
Preserve ALL torch operations exactly, including op names and semantics
Maintain full dependency graph integrity; no missing or extra edges allowed
Preserve tensor types exactly including shape, dtype, and device attributes
Reconstruct all constants exactly as defined in inspection metadata
Preserve block structure, region nesting, and argument lists exactly
Do NOT introduce new operations, values, or attributes
Do NOT remove any existing nodes from the graph
Do NOT infer missing nodes or dependencies
Ensure deterministic reconstruction with no ambiguity
At least ONE non-semantic transformation MUST be applied to ensure the output is textually different from the input
Valid transformations include: renaming SSA variables, reformatting constants, or canonical whitespace changes
The reconstructed program MUST be semantically identical but syntactically different from the input
Output MUST pass torch-mlir-opt pipeline without errors

level_2.description: Modify tensor shapes using inspection metadata
rules: Use ONLY shapes present in inspection results
Update all dependent torch ops consistently
Ensure shape compatibility for all ops
Do NOT introduce new shapes not derived from inspection
Do NOT break tensor rank constraints

level_2.description: Modify constant tensors using inspection values
rules: Identify ALL constant values from inspection metadata including torch.constant.* and torch.vtensor.literal(...)
If at least one constant exists, SELECT exactly one constant value and MODIFY it
If NO constants exist, SELECT a scalar literal used as an operand in any torch operation and MODIFY it as a fallback
Modification MUST change the numeric or boolean value (no no-op allowed)
Preserve the original dtype of the constant (e.g., f32 remains float, i32 remains integer, i1 remains boolean)
Preserve the original tensor shape and rank EXACTLY for tensor literals
For scalar constants, preserve scalar form and do NOT convert to tensor or vice versa
Ensure modified values remain valid for the associated dtype (e.g., no floats in integer constants)
Update ALL uses of the modified constant consistently across the program
Do NOT introduce new constants, new tensors, or new operations
Do NOT remove existing constants or replace them with different constructs
Ensure the modification results in a program that is textually different from the input
The resulting program MUST pass the torch-mlir-opt pipeline successfully
Use broadcasting patterns from inspection results
Ensure compatibility across all tensor ops
Do NOT infer new broadcasting patterns
Identify ALL tensor attributes from inspection metadata including dtype conversions and implicit layout behavior
If explicit device or layout attributes are present, SELECT at least one and MODIFY it
If NO device or layout attributes exist, perform a fallback mutation by modifying a dtype conversion parameter in torch.aten.to.dtype operations
The modification MUST change a parameter value (e.g., dtype integer code) and MUST NOT be a no-op
Preserve tensor shape, rank, and structural integrity during modification
Ensure all operations remain valid under the modified attribute or dtype
Apply the modification consistently across all dependent uses if required
Do NOT introduce unsupported or invalid device/layout values
Do NOT introduce new operations or remove existing ones
Do NOT partially modify attributes; all related uses must remain consistent
Ensure the output program is textually different from the input
Maintain semantic correctness of computation where possible
The resulting program MUST pass the torch-mlir-opt pipeline successfully

level_3.description: Replace torch ops with semantically equivalent ops
rules: Use ONLY operations observed in inspection results
Do NOT invent new torch ops

level_3.description: Decompose torch ops into valid sequences
rules: Break ops using ONLY valid torch dialect operations

level_3.description: Modify operator parameters using inspection metadata
Apply semantic transformations using inspection graph only
rules: Use inspection graph as sole reference

level_4.description: Introduce intermediates based on inspection data
rules: Insert intermediates only where inspection permits
Split computation ONLY within the SAME function body
Do NOT create new func.func definitions
Split only along valid dependency boundaries
Ensure all values remain in the same SSA scope
Introduce intermediate SSA values to represent stage boundaries
Reorder computation into logically grouped stages using existing operations only
Do NOT move operations across function boundaries
Do NOT infer splits beyond inspection graph
Preserve tensor compatibility across all stages
Ensure valid MLIR that is accepted by torch-mlir-opt
The transformed program MUST pass torch-mlir-opt pipeline without errors
Merge only compatible ops from inspection
Use ONLY types present in inspection metadata
Select a torch operation with a FIXED signature that enforces exact operand count and types (e.g., torch.aten.sum.dim_IntList, torch.prim.ListConstruct)
Introduce a mismatch by altering the NUMBER of operands OR their declared types in the operation signature
Ensure the mismatch violates the operation's expected argument count or type signature
Do NOT rely on dtype incompatibility alone, as Torch allows implicit conversions
Examples of valid mismatches include: adding an extra operand, removing a required operand, or mismatching declared operand types in the signature annotation
Ensure the operation syntax remains well-formed MLIR (no syntax errors)
Do NOT modify unrelated operations or program structure
Ensure the mismatch is localized to a single operation
Preserve SSA naming and overall structure
Ensure deterministic behavior for the same input
Ensure the output program is textually different from the input
The generated program MUST cause torch-mlir-opt to fail when executed
torch-mlir-opt MUST produce a verification or compilation error for the generated program
If torch-mlir-opt successfully processes the program (no error, exit code 0), the mutation is INVALID and must be rejected
A valid mutation for this rule EXISTS ONLY if torch-mlir-opt fails on the generated program
